NWS storm survey team confirmed an EF-0 tornado with an estimated peak wind speed of 85 mph near the intersection of Clito Rd and Rough Rider Rd in eastern Bulloch County. The tornado occurred from 2:12 PM to 2:13 PM. Please see the Public Information Statement for additional details.
Picture of ongoing tornado near Effingham Highway.
Picture of ongoing tornado near Effingham Highway. Spotter noted trees were being shredded by the tornado.

NWS Survey Team confirmed an EF-0 tornado south southeast of Captolo_ GA. A weak tornado briefly touched down near Wind Mill Road_ southeast of Captolo_ GA_ before moving north-northeast and dissipating just north of Limesink Road. Its track was periodically visible across open grass fields. Tornado damage was minor and limited to the breakage of large branches from both hardwood and softwood trees. The tin roof was pealed back on a standalone garage.
A 911 call center reported roof damage possibly to multiple homes near Hilltop Lane at Savannah Hwy. A downed power pole was also reported. Damage was likely due to a tornado.

NWS Survey Team confirmed an EF-1 tornado in eastern Screven County_ GA. The tornado touched down just south of Hwy 21 near Ogeechee Creek before dissipating just north of Old Poor Robin Road. It produced significant tree damage along its path with numerous large hardwood and softwood trees being either snapped off or completely uprooted. One mobile home suffered major damage as a large hardwood tree fell on it. Several cars were also crushed from trees falling on them.
Fire Chief reports tornado on the ground near Highway 21_ causing tree tops to be shredded. Live stream video also shows downed trees and debris being lofted into the air.
Numerous trees and power poles downed near Old Savannah Hwy and Hwy 21 likely due to tornado. Damage was estimated to be about 200 yards wide.
Fire Chief reports trees down on mobile home. No injuries reported.

SCEMD reported four homes located along the 11000 block of Burtons Ferry Hwy with damage likely due to a tornado. They reported three of the homes with major damage and one destroyed. No injuries were reported. Time was estimated via radar data.
Live stream showed active tornado on the ground_ causing trees to be shredded and debris to be lofted. Roof and siding were also ripped off manufactured home_ and power lines were snapped.

NWS Survey Team confirmed an EF-1 tornado in western Allendale Co. The tornado crossed Hwy 301 west of Gravel Hill Rd_ causing significant damage. 4 homes were impacted: one sustained destruction of aluminum roofing material and a front porch; one had complete roof & outer wall failure on a rear addition; & 2 sustained minor roof damage. An outbuilding & 2 carports were destroyed. The tornado continued north with additional tree damage west of Moultry Loop and on Revolutionary Trail.

NWS Survey Team confired an EF-1 tornado in northern Allendale County. A tornado touched down in the wooded area between Miller Creek Road and Yackin Road_ rapidly moving north across Camp Jackson Road. It dissipated just east of the Camp Jackson facility_ short of the Barnwell County line. Impact was primarily limited to forested areas_ with high winds snapping and uprooting clusters of hardwood and softwood trees.
911 call center reported numerous trees and power lines down along Miller Creek Rd. Damage was likely due to a tornado. Time was estimated via radar data.
Tornado crossing Miller Creek Rd on live stream_ which resulted in downed trees and powerlines.
Buoy 41004 measured a 35 knot wind gust at 5:50 am. A peak wind gust of 37 knots was measured at 6:00 am.
